quotes: "Currently AI code generation tools lack a evaluation mechanism for the quality and correctness of the AI-suggested code, as P3 observed with the example of Copilot, “GitHub Copilot just hands you the code, and it’s up to you to know whether or not that’s good code.”" (p. 14)

paper_code_entries.value: process — the study elicited imagined use, needs, reactions, and workflow implications rather than artifact quality or learning outcomes (PDF p. 18).
quotes: "We used the stimuli to elicit user experience, needs, and feedback." (p. 18)

paper_code_entries.value: structuring — the design organizes community evidence into glanceable indicators with optional drill-down (PDF p. 23).
quotes: "For example, information could be presented in a hierarchical manner—users may first take a glance at some sort of indicators, perhaps in the form of icons or numerical scales, that can quickly tell them what is going on in the community about a particular AI suggestion." (p. 23)

paper_code_entries.value: problematizing — diverse peer examples make both AI successes and failures visible so the developer must confront uncertainty rather than assume uniform capability (PDF p. 22).
quotes: "With community-curated experiences, developers are exposed to diverse examples of how AI can work or fail in different use cases, which complements their individual understanding of the trust affordances." (p. 22)

paper_code_entries.value: distributed_support — evaluation is spread across the developer’s expertise, community signals, community discussion, and the AI-assisted environment (PDF p. 23).
quotes: "These signals can serve as heuristics in addition to the developers’ own expertise, scaffolding them to effectively evaluate an AI suggestion and make decisions on whether to trust it." (p. 23)

paper_code_entries.value: none_comparator_only — the scaffold’s meaning is supplied by community members and deterministic aggregation, although it concerns AI-generated suggestions (PDF p. 13).
quotes: "We refer to these contributions of community members as community-generated evaluation signals." (p. 13)

paper_code_entries.value: pre_ai_computational — the support layer consists of conventional community statistics, voting, search, video, metadata, and discussion rather than model-generated meaning (PDF p. 16).
quotes: "We introduced feature A Community usage statistics and feature B community voting as indicators of code quality that allow users to see the prevalence of the suggestion used by other users, the percentage of acceptance, edits, rejection, and passing of downstream tests, as well as votings in terms of likes and shares." (p. 16)

limitations: "We also do not claim that the designs presented in the stimuli are the best solution to the problems." (p. 18)
"However, we cannot claim that the findings will apply to all possible AI applications and to all domains in which AI is applied." (p. 24)
"Second, this research is based on 17 interviews with software developers and 11 design probe sessions and could be considered a formative study." (p. 24)
"Although we have discovered a rich set of insights from our qualitative work, future work should focus on more quantitative analysis of trust and communities with a larger study population." (p. 24)
"The study was conducted at a time when Copilot was just released and people started adopting Copilot." (p. 24)
"Of the 17 participants in Study 1, only two were women, while the rest were all men and no gender-nonconforming participants were recruited." (p. 24)
boundary_conditions: "Fourth, this research was focused on current software developers, and we intentionally included participants with a range of years of programming experience." (p. 25)
